title: Sizes that cannot overflow
description:
Compute buffer sizes from untrusted counts without overflowing.

```
count 1000, size 16 -> 16000
count 0x20000000, size 16 -> refused (overflows 32 bits)
header 12 + count * 16 with count 0xFFFFFFFF -> refused
```
hints: `a != 0 && b > max / a` means `a * b` would overflow (lesson 17.04).
Doing the multiply in 64 bits and checking against the 32-bit maximum works too.
requirements: `std::optional<std::uint32_t> checkedMul(a, b)` and `checkedAdd` for unsigned 32-bit values.
Test the edge values: 0, 1, the maximum, and just over it.
